**CPU (Central Processing Unit)**  
| Feature | Typical Use‑Case |
|---------|------------------|
| **Design Goal** | General‑purpose processing – handle a wide variety of tasks quickly with low latency. |
| **Core Count & Size** | Small number of powerful cores (2–32 on most consumer CPUs). Each core can execute complex instructions independently. |
| **Instruction Set** | Rich, versatile instruction set (x86, ARM, etc.) capable of branching, floating‑point math, integer ops, SIMD extensions, cryptography, etc. |
| **Memory Hierarchy** | Large caches per core (L1/L2/L3) and tight integration with main memory; very fast context switching. |
| **Typical Workloads** | Operating system kernels, application logic, database queries, web servers, gaming engines’ control flow, AI inference frameworks when not heavily parallelized. |

---

### GPU (Graphics Processing Unit)

| Feature | Typical Use‑Case |
|---------|------------------|
| **Design Goal** | Massive data‑parallel throughput—perform the same operation many times over thousands of elements simultaneously. |
| **Core Count & Size** | Thousands of lightweight “stream” or CUDA cores/ALUs. They’re simpler but highly efficient at executing identical operations in lockstep. |
| **Instruction Set** | Specialized for vector/matrix arithmetic, texture sampling, rasterization, ray tracing primitives, tensor math, etc. |
| **Memory Hierarchy** | Smaller per‑core cache; relies on high bandwidth global VRAM and shared memory blocks within thread groups (“warps”). |
| **Typical Workloads** | Rendering graphics pipelines, scientific simulations, deep learning training/inference, video encoding/decoding, cryptocurrency mining, big‑data analytics where the same calculation repeats across huge datasets. |

---

#### Key Differences Summarised

| Aspect | CPU | GPU |
|--------|-----|-----|
| **Parallelism Model** | Few, serially‑oriented threads → *task* parallelism | Many, SIMT (Single Instruction Multiple Threads) → *data* parallelism |
| **Latency vs Throughput** | Low latency, high single‑thread performance | High throughput, higher latency per individual task |
| **Branch Prediction / Control Flow** | Excellent branch prediction, handles divergent code well | Poor handling of branches; best when all threads follow the same path |
| **Power Efficiency** | Optimised for diverse workloads, moderate power draw | Very energy‑efficient for massive parallel work, but overall consumption rises sharply with workload size |
| **Programming Models** | C/C++, Java, Rust, .NET, etc.; standard OS APIs | CUDA/OpenCL/Vulkan/SPIR-V, specialized libraries like cuBLAS/TensorRT, Metal Performance Shaders |

In practice, modern systems use both together: the CPU orchestrates general program flow while delegating heavy, repetitive calculations to the GPU. This hybrid approach gives you the flexibility of a CPU plus the raw speed of a GPU for suitable problems.
